title: Vaishnavism Saints Dadu Dayal
definition: Dadu Dayal (1544–1603) was a prominent 16th-century Nirguna Bhakti saint from Rajasthan, who founded the Dadu Panth, emphasizing monotheism, social equality, and the rejection of caste-based rituals.
importanceInUpsc: UPSC frequently tests the Bhakti movement's regional variations, the distinction between Saguna/Nirguna traditions, and the socio-religious impact of saints like Dadu Dayal on medieval Indian society.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Vaishnavism Saints Dadu Dayal.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of Bhakti Movement
Understanding of Nirguna vs Saguna traditions
